subject: CloudNova: request for temporary Dedicated ramp + autoscale safeguard
messages:
From: Samir Rao <ops@cloudnova.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudnova.com (Elena Mendez)
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short-term ramp request for Jan 26-30 model sweep

Hi Stephanie and Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We have an internal commitment to run a large model-sweep the week of Jan 26 to validate final quantization settings before we expand our Dedicated contract. That sweep will temporarily multiply token throughput by ~8x for 48 hours.

Can Redwood support a temporary reserved carve (or a soft carve with guaranteed fallback) for 48 hours (Jan 26 00:00 PST through Jan 27 23:59 PST)? Two specific asks:
- A temporary reservation of ~8x baseline GPU slots for the window, or an autoscale-safeguard that prevents other noisy tenants from evicting our running experiments.
- A rollback/fallback plan if we exceed the window so our live product is not impacted.

We want to avoid committing long-term until we confirm the end-to-end perf profile, but a short-term safety lane will let us complete the evaluation. I attached a short scope doc describing the sweep and expected token volume.

Can we get a quick ops+product decision this week? We need to confirm procurement language (dates) to get internal approvals.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Ops, CloudNova
(attachment: CloudNova_Scope.pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <ops@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short-term ramp request for Jan 26-30 model sweep

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the scope doc. Laura and I will triage from product/ops; looping in Karthik and Marissa for infra and resourcing. A couple quick clarifying questions for the team so we can evaluate tradeoffs: 

- Is the 8x an instantaneous peak (bursty for a few hours) or sustained over full 48h?
- Do you require strict eviction protection (hard carve) or would a prioritized soft carve with guaranteed fallback to a lower-capacity model be acceptable?
- Any ATO/compliance constraints for telemetry during that window?

Assuming we can get those answers, we can propose either a short-term reservation or a prioritized autoscale policy with a temporary SLO relaxation and an automated rollback. I propose a 30-minute sync Thursday to lock the runway.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <ops@cloudnova.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short-term ramp request for Jan 26-30 model sweep

Stephanie / Laura — technical note + constraints.

Quick answers to Samir's clarifications: from the scope, the 8x looks like a 6–10 hour sustained peak each day (not constant 48h), with a few smaller bursts outside that window. That pattern helps with scheduling, but it still risks eviction under current fairshare.

Options we can offer: 
1) Hard carve: allocate a dedicated slice (reserved slots) for the two-day window. Pros: predictable. Cons: operationally expensive and requires approval from capacity stewarding; we'd need to preempt other pilots.
2) Soft prioritized carve: higher scheduler weight + autoscale-safeguard flag to avoid preemption for active jobs that present the flag; automatic degradation path (route new requests to a quantized/cheaper model variant after a token threshold). Pros: lower impact to other customers, quicker to approve. Cons: risk of degraded quality if fallback fires.

For either path we need: a precise expected token budget, an explicit start/end (UTC aligned), and an emergency rollback contact list (oncall + CloudNova ops). Also need a short runbook that states what triggers rollback (latency > 500ms for >5 minutes, or cost > agreed threshold).

Dev — can you confirm if we can enable the autoscale-safeguard flag for a named customer in the Hosted scheduling layer for Jan 26-27 and program the fallback routing? If not, we escalate for a temporary hard carve.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <ops@cloudnova.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Decision: approved soft-priority carve with rollback gates (Jan 26-27) — next steps

Samir / team — thanks for the patience and the details you shared. Summary of the decision from product + infra: we will grant a prioritized soft carve for Jan 26 00:00 PST through Jan 27 23:59 PST with the following controls: 

- Reservation type: prioritized soft carve (no hard GPU reservation).
- Scheduler change: enable autoscale-safeguard flag for CloudNova tenant id (INF-9452) to prevent preemption of active jobs during their peak windows.
- Token budget: CloudNova to confirm a hard token cap of 1.6B tokens across the window; exceeding that will trigger automated reroute to quantized-model variant v2-q4o.
- Rollback gates: latency > 500ms sustained for 5m OR error rate > 2% sustained 5m will trigger automated traffic shift to the fallback model and email alerts to both parties.
- Escalation contacts: Redwood oncall + Karthik; CloudNova ops: Samir Rao, Elena Mendez.
- Procurement note: Laura will confirm language allowing this single short-term carve without long-term capacity commitment.

Actions and owners:
- Samir: confirm token cap number and provide finalized contact list (by EOD 1/22).
- Dev: enable autoscale-safeguard flag and schedule rollout for 1/25 22:00 PST; confirm fallback routing works in staging (INF-9452).
- Marissa: draft brief runbook (runbook-draft.md) and post to the shared Drive; include rollback steps and dashboard links.
- Laura: finalize procurement wording and notify finance if any provisional credits are needed.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CloudNovaPilot — runbook and scope live there; JIRA INF-9452 tracks infra work.

I will keep this thread for final confirmations. If CloudNova confirms the token cap by EOD Friday we are green to go.

Thanks — Stephanie
